chunks: Then turned his back and waxed proud,

key_terms.أَدْبَرَ: Turned his back; to turn away in rejection or departure
key_terms.اسْتَکْبَرَ: Waxed proud; to become arrogant or haughty

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Then turned his back and waxed proud' signify in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this phrase encapsulates the archetype of *istikbar* (arrogance) as a spiritual blindness that prevents recognition of divine truth, often linked to Pharaoh's rejection of Musa. The turning away signifies not just physical departure but an internal hardening of the heart, a state where pride overrides reason and revelation. This reaction serves as a cautionary model for believers to avoid the same spiritual stagnation when confronted with the guidance of the Ahl al-Bayt.
